method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)' (first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027), 19 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0. eviQ also states that its content should not be hosted on external sites, and that commercial entities must contact eviQ to seek permission (https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright). Adaptations must cite the eviQ ID, version and URL. (read at https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright (Disclaimer and copyright page)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and GEICO; Ramirez et al., Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04046-1) 'SEOM-GEICO clinical guidelines on endometrial cancer (2025)' (published online 23 September 2025), 12 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12630260). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps every eviQ claim (S1) unchanged and adds S2, the SEOM-GEICO 2025 endometrial cancer guideline (a national society guideline, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, paraphrased), for the treatment pathway around the eviQ regimen: MMR and HER2 testing, chemotherapy backbone, pMMR options, hormonal therapy, later lines and follow-up. Its tables and algorithm were stripped; only running text is used. The ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2025 update (Lancet Oncology) is not open on Europe PMC. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S2 Table 1 (diagnosis and staging recommendations with grades) and Table 3 (FIGO 2023 staging, stages III-IV) added; S2 Table 2 (ragged rows) and Table 4 (merged cells) were not extracted. S1 (eviQ) is a web page with no appended tables.

claims.claim: **For dMMR endometrial cancer (mismatch repair deficient on immunohistochemistry) that is advanced, metastatic or recurrent**, and either untreated with systemic therapy or relapsing more than 6 months after the last neoadjuvant or adjuvant systemic treatment.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No earlier anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 drug for this indication, and ECOG performance status 0 or 1.**
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Talk to an expert first** if the patient has significant autoimmune disease, an organ transplant, previous viral hepatitis or past lung irradiation.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Only specialists experienced with immunotherapy should start and supervise treatment**, and they must be confident in managing immune-related adverse events.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **PBS status:** dostarlimab is a PBS authority item for dMMR endometrial cancer only; for pMMR disease it is TGA-registered but not PBS-listed. Carboplatin and paclitaxel are on the general schedule.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cycles 1 to 6, every 21 days, all on day 1:** dostarlimab 500 mg IV, paclitaxel 175 mg/m² IV and carboplatin AUC 5 IV. **From cycle 7:** dostarlimab 1,000 mg IV every 42 days, until progression, unacceptable toxicity or a maximum of 3 years.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Carboplatin is dosed by the Calvert formula, ideally with a measured GFR** when intent is curative or estimates may mislead: eGFR above 125 or at or below 45 mL/min/1.73 m², extremes of body size or muscle mass, amputation or paraplegia. Otherwise a BSA-adjusted eGFR is acceptable.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recalculate the carboplatin dose only if kidney function shifts by more than 20% from baseline or the patient's condition changes.**
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Early growth may be pseudoprogression** (rare, about 5%): if the patient seems to be benefiting, consider carrying on and repeating the scan 4 to 6 weeks later. Radiation recall is possible, so time the start carefully after a long radiotherapy course.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hypersensitivity risk is high with both paclitaxel and carboplatin.** Carboplatin reactions become likelier with each cycle and premedication may not stop them; rechallenge after a reaction needs a desensitisation protocol with support on hand.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Immune-related adverse events can start early, worsen quickly and appear even after treatment stops; deaths have occurred.** The most dangerous include myocarditis, HLH-like syndrome, myositis, encephalitis, Guillain-Barré syndrome, myelitis, myasthenia gravis, pneumonitis and SJS/TEN. Monitor proactively, encourage early self-reporting, and interrupt treatment, consult specialists and give corticosteroids as required.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Baseline tests:** FBC, EUC, eGFR, LFTs, calcium, magnesium, cortisol, TFTs and glucose; consider ECG, troponin and urinalysis. **Each cycle:** FBC, EUC, eGFR, LFTs and glucose. TFTs (and consider cortisol) every 4-6 weeks on treatment and every 12 weeks afterwards as indicated; lipase and amylase if pancreatitis is suspected.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen everyone for hepatitis before a checkpoint inhibitor.** Patients with chronic hepatitis B or C, a detectable HIV viral load or AIDS need close monitoring and antiviral treatment if indicated.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dostarlimab is not dose-reduced.** No change is needed for older age or mild hepatic impairment; checkpoint inhibitors are unstudied in moderate to severe hepatic impairment.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Blood counts before each cycle:** delay for ANC 0.5 to under 1.0 or platelets 50 to under 75; for ANC under 0.5, platelets under 50 or febrile neutropenia, delay, and consider a 25% cut to both paclitaxel and carboplatin for later cycles.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Paclitaxel:** cut by 25% for mild and 50% for moderate hepatic dysfunction, and omit if severe. Grade 2 neuropathy at the next cycle: delay until grade 1 or better, then reduce paclitaxel by 25%, stopping it if the delay passes 3 weeks or neuropathy returns. Grade 3 or 4 neuropathy: omit paclitaxel.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Classify every endometrial cancer molecularly** for sharper risk grouping and treatment choice [III, A], and assess for hereditary syndromes, offering genetic counselling to those who test positive [III, A] (S2 summary table).
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and GEICO; Ramirez et al., Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04046-1), 'SEOM-GEICO clinical guidelines on endometrial cancer (2025)', published online 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12630260/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Stage III under FIGO 2023 (S2 Table 3)** is regional spread of any histology: IIIA1 ovary or fallopian tube (unless it meets IA3), IIIA2 uterine subserosa or through the serosa, IIIB1 parametria and/or vagina, IIIB2 pelvic peritoneum, IIIC1 pelvic nodes and IIIC2 para-aortic nodes up to the renal vessels, each nodal stage split into micro- and macrometastasis.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and GEICO; Ramirez et al., Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04046-1), 'SEOM-GEICO clinical guidelines on endometrial cancer (2025)', published online 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12630260/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Stage IV under FIGO 2023:** IVA bladder or bowel mucosa, IVB peritoneal spread beyond the pelvis, IVC distant metastasis including nodes above the renal vessels. Molecular class (POLEmut or p53abn) changes the stage only in stages I and II, not III or IV, but should still be recorded. Macrometastases are over 2 mm; micrometastases 0.2–2 mm and/or over 200 cells.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and GEICO; Ramirez et al., Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04046-1), 'SEOM-GEICO clinical guidelines on endometrial cancer (2025)', published online 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12630260/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Test every endometrial cancer for mismatch repair deficiency by immunohistochemistry** (Lynch syndrome screening, whatever the age or histology) [II, A]; MLH1 loss needs MLH1 promoter methylation (or BRAF) testing before germline analysis. Also assess ER at diagnosis [IV, A], because it predicts response to hormonal treatment in advanced disease.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and GEICO; Ramirez et al., Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04046-1), 'SEOM-GEICO clinical guidelines on endometrial cancer (2025)', published online 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12630260/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Isolated pelvic recurrence or a single metastatic site:** consider surgery, radiotherapy or ablation [IV, A], followed by systemic treatment of uncertain benefit [IV, B]. Unresectable or metastatic disease is treated with chemotherapy, immunotherapy or hormonal therapy, and trial enrolment is strongly encouraged [V, B].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and GEICO; Ramirez et al., Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04046-1), 'SEOM-GEICO clinical guidelines on endometrial cancer (2025)', published online 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12630260/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **The chemotherapy backbone is carboplatin AUC 5–6 with paclitaxel 175 mg/m² every three weeks** [I, A]: in GOG 209 it was non-inferior to the three-drug TAP regimen (PFS 12–14 months, OS 32 months) and less toxic.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and GEICO; Ramirez et al., Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04046-1), 'SEOM-GEICO clinical guidelines on endometrial cancer (2025)', published online 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12630260/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **dMMR first line (S2): chemotherapy with a checkpoint inhibitor, then checkpoint maintenance, is standard** [I, A]: pembrolizumab for 2 years (NRG-GY018, dMMR PFS HR 0.3) or dostarlimab for 3 years (RUBY, dMMR PFS HR 0.23 and OS HR 0.32). Atezolizumab and durvalumab have also shown first-line activity. The two trials differ in design (interval since adjuvant therapy, maintenance length, histologies included), which matters when choosing.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and GEICO; Ramirez et al., Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04046-1), 'SEOM-GEICO clinical guidelines on endometrial cancer (2025)', published online 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12630260/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **pMMR first line (S2): chemotherapy plus immunotherapy is also the standard** [I, B], though the gain is smaller than in dMMR. Adding a PARP inhibitor to chemotherapy and immunotherapy (RUBY part 2, DUO-E) is another option for pMMR [I, B]. Lenvatinib with pembrolizumab failed as first line (LEAP-001), but may be considered for pMMR relapse after adjuvant chemotherapy when more chemotherapy is contraindicated [III, C].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and GEICO; Ramirez et al., Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04046-1), 'SEOM-GEICO clinical guidelines on endometrial cancer (2025)', published online 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12630260/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Hormonal therapy suits low-grade, hormone receptor-positive disease that is not rapidly progressing or bulky** [II, A]: megestrol acetate 160 mg daily or medroxyprogesterone acetate 200 mg daily (preferred), alone or with tamoxifen, or tamoxifen, an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant [III, A]. Consider rebiopsy at recurrence to confirm receptor status [IV, B]; responses are about 10–25% in chemotherapy-naive patients.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and GEICO; Ramirez et al., Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04046-1), 'SEOM-GEICO clinical guidelines on endometrial cancer (2025)', published online 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12630260/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Second line after platinum, if no prior immunotherapy:** dMMR: dostarlimab or pembrolizumab alone [III, A] (response rates 46% in GARNET and 57% in KEYNOTE-158), or pembrolizumab with lenvatinib [I, B]. pMMR: pembrolizumab with lenvatinib [I, A], which beat chemotherapy on PFS, OS and response whatever the MMR status, at the cost of frequent hypertension, hypothyroidism and diarrhoea.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and GEICO; Ramirez et al., Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04046-1), 'SEOM-GEICO clinical guidelines on endometrial cancer (2025)', published online 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12630260/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **After immunotherapy,** options are modest (weekly paclitaxel, docetaxel, oxaliplatin, liposomal doxorubicin, topotecan, ifosfamide), and platinum can be repeated after a late relapse. **Test HER2:** about 30% of serous carcinomas are HER2-positive; trastuzumab added to carboplatin-paclitaxel improved PFS and OS, and trastuzumab deruxtecan gave an 84% response rate in strongly HER2-expressing (+++) endometrial cancer (phase II).
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and GEICO; Ramirez et al., Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04046-1), 'SEOM-GEICO clinical guidelines on endometrial cancer (2025)', published online 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12630260/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Follow-up:** review every three to six months for two years, then every six to twelve months, with symptom review and a speculum and bimanual examination; teach the symptoms of recurrence. Serum markers and routine vaginal cytology are not recommended [I, A].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and GEICO; Ramirez et al., Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04046-1), 'SEOM-GEICO clinical guidelines on endometrial cancer (2025)', published online 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12630260/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **The supporting trial is RUBY (phase III, 487 patients)** with primary stage III-IV or first recurrent endometrial cancer, untreated or relapsing at least 6 months after adjuvant or neoadjuvant therapy. Patients had carboplatin and paclitaxel with dostarlimab or placebo for six cycles, then dostarlimab 1000 mg or placebo 6-weekly, for a maximum of 3 years.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The benefit was concentrated in dMMR/MSI-H disease:** 24-month PFS 61.4% vs 15.7% (HR 0.28) and 36-month OS 78.0% vs 46.0% (HR 0.32). Overall, 24-month PFS was 36.1% vs 18.1% (HR 0.64) with an OS HR of 0.69. In pMMR disease the PFS HR was 0.76 and the OS HR 0.79, with a confidence interval that included no effect.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Serious treatment-related adverse events were commoner with dostarlimab (19.5% vs 12.2%), and so were stops for adverse events (19.1% vs 8.1%).** Nausea, alopecia and fatigue were the most frequent events in both arms.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4423 Endometrial recurrent or metastatic carboplatin, paclitaxel and dostarlimab (eviQ ID 4423, version 2)', first approved 21 August 2024; last reviewed 15 December 2025; review due 31 December 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4423, retrieved 2026-09-23
